sections.label: Our Teams

briefs.headline: Tottenham beaten 2-0 at home by Newcastle, still pointless
briefs.summary: Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa scored in a ten-minute second-half stretch Saturday in London; Spurs have lost both league matches and sit bottom of the table.

briefs.headline: Liverpool twice behind, twice level in 2-2 with Forest
briefs.summary: Dan Ndoye and a Morgan Gibbs-White penalty had Forest ahead at Anfield Saturday before Victor Munoz leveled in the 82nd; Andoni Iraola is still without a win after two draws.

briefs.headline: Reds routed 17-5 at Wrigley as Crow-Armstrong homers three times
briefs.summary: Pete Crow-Armstrong drove in six Saturday, a day after Cincinnati took the series opener; the Reds are last in the NL Central with a month left.

briefs.headline: Pirates break out for a 6-2 win in St. Louis
briefs.summary: Rafael Flores Jr.'s three-run homer and a Brandon Lowe solo shot backed six pitchers Saturday; a team that had scored eight runs in six games held St. Louis to three hits.

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati blanked 4-0 by East-leading Nashville
briefs.summary: Sam Surridge, Hany Mukhtar and two late goals did it at Geodis Park Saturday; Cincinnati stay sixth in the East as Nashville pull clear on top.

briefs.headline: Both Marshall soccer sides draw on the road
briefs.summary: The No. 12 men held UC Santa Barbara 1-1 Thursday on Thiago Apolinario's goal; the women drew 3-3 at Belmont on Wiktoria Mikrut's hat trick, the program's tenth.

sections.label: Around the Leagues

briefs.headline: NFL teams cut to 53 by 6 tonight, on a Sunday for the first time
briefs.summary: All 32 rosters, the Browns' and Bengals' included, are due down from 90 by 6 p.m. ET; waiver claims process Monday at 1 p.m., and practice squads of up to 17 build after that.

briefs.headline: Banzuke day is tomorrow; September's dates are still the JSA's to name
briefs.summary: Monday's autumn rankings release is when the association must finally put citable dates on the Aki basho - its English site still shows September sold out with no schedule posted, and the derived Sept. 13 opening, two weeks out, remains unconfirmed.

sections.label: In Season

coming_in.item: Opens TUESDAY in joint and coastal waters: one fish per day, 15-inch minimum, with mandatory harvest reporting. NCDMF is also collecting donated carcasses for age-and-growth science, with prizes drawn from donors.
The youth weekend runs Saturday and Sunday, daily bag 6; the general season follows Sept. 12 and runs to Feb. 28.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

prime.item: Coastal waters: an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one per day; unlawful to possess a fish over 27 inches.
Coastal waters: a 14-to-20-inch slot, three per day, of which one may exceed 26 inches.

going_out.item: The first gun window, open since Saturday in SELECTED COUNTIES only, closes a week from Monday - the county list is not in the pamphlet's summary table, so none is named here. Daily 1, season limit 2; electronic registration required.
going_out.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

sections.note: The DNR's separate migratory bird summary is still untranscribed in this repo, so no dove or goose date prints. WV trout stocking is a January-May program; the summer search came back empty, as expected.

waters.working: Half of yesterday's 350 and dropping - the river is fishable again and clearing. Pocket water and plunge-pool seams on a dry-dropper, a caddis up top with a small stonefly nymph trailing; the sculpin bite fades as the color leaves.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.0 ft - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Settled at pool - shad are the forage, so a white swimbait worked across the wing-dam seams early, then a jig dragged slower as the sun climbs.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.8 ft - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Steady and clearing below the dam - a crawfish crankbait ticked along the riprap and lock wall, and a jig to the barge cuts for fish holding off the current.

waters.reading: Sound highs 10:27 AM at 3.8 ft and 10:43 PM at 3.8 ft at Hampstead; lows 4:35 AM at 0.4 ft and 4:58 PM at 0.7 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 10:27 AM and 10:43 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Waning gibbous at 94%, springs easing toward neap, but the ebb off the 10:27 high into the 4:58 PM low is still the red drum window on the oyster bars and grass edges, cut menhaden off the channel lips. Water 81.9F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast. The Fisherman's Post monthly, published Aug. 2 and four weeks old, has the surf giving up whiting and black drum on shrimp, the piers throwing tarpon and 3-pound Spanish - and flounder opens here Tuesday, one a day at 15 inches.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and the read that matters; the oceanfront pier runs well ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. No watches, warnings or advisories posted for the Topsail area this morning per the National Weather Service.

kicker: Flounder opens Tuesday on the coast; the banzuke lands tomorrow, and the NFL cuts to 53 by tonight.
